items.title: BMS reveals death from septic pneumonia of multiple sclerosis patient in CAR T trial
items.snippet: The disclosure—which came ahead of a presentation of data from the Phase 1 Breakfree-2 study at the ACTRIMS-ECTRIMS meeting—follows Bristol Myers Squibb’s late summer revelation that it had paused certain trials of zolacabtagene autoleucel.

items.title: Alnylam plans pivotal trial as Huntington’s drug notches ‘best-in-class knockdown’
items.snippet: RNAi specialist Alnylam Pharmaceuticals will advance the Huntington’s disease drug brezosiran into a placebo-controlled study in 2027 once regulatory alignment is achieved.

items.title: ESMO 2026: Tango trips on sinking response rates in pancreatic cancer but will move to Phase 3
items.snippet: A combination of Tango Therapeutics’ vopimetostat and Revolution Medicines’ recently approved Rasonque led to a response rate of 82% in an ongoing Phase 1/2 trial—a drop from 92% that was reported in June in fewer patients.

items.title: Tango plans 14% workforce cut, mainly of research staff
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: Roche flags ‘final opportunity’ for Germany to reestablish as a reliable investment location
items.snippet: Following the withdrawal of billions of dollars in investments from Boehringer Ingelheim and Eli Lilly, German lawmakers have proposed a clause to the country’s healthcare reforms set to take effect Jan. 1.

items.title: Gilead shops in IL-23, inking $1.3B upfront I&I deal with China’s PepStar
items.snippet: Gilead Sciences has picked up a new inflammatory disease program from China’s PepStar Therapeutics to pair with the Phase 2 inflammatory bowel disease asset emvistegrast.

items.title: ESMO 2026: Marengo's bispecific antibody shrinks 8 tumor types in Phase 2
items.snippet: Invikafusp alfa, a first-in-class dual T cell agonist, showed an objective response in various types of cancer, particularly among patients who did not respond to previous checkpoint inhibitor therapy.

items.title: US explores China biotech restrictions, exempts licensing deals
items.snippet: A new proposal from the U.S. government seeking to address investment in Chinese biotech as a matter of national security drew cautious statements from across the industry, with leaders vowing to ensure innovation isn’t stifled.

items.title: FDA uncages Aardvark’s Prader-Willi study after new data cleared safety concerns
items.snippet: After cardiac safety signals led to a full clinical hold on Aardvark Therapeutics’ studies of ARD-101, the biotech conducted an additional safety study, in which no cardiac events were detected. Aardvark plans to resume testing the candidate next year.

items.title: Roche bets up to $813M on Zymeworks’ lung cancer trispecific T cell engager
items.snippet: Roche will pay Zymeworks $55 million upfront plus another $40 million once the partnership asset enters Phase 1b development and up to $718 million in additional milestones.

items.title: ESMO 2026: Merck, Moderna shares fall as cancer vaccine disappoints after data leak
items.snippet: A combination of the personalized cancer vaccine intismeran autogene and Merck's Keytruda just barely cleared analysts’ expectations for recurrence-free survival, leaving questions as to its applicability to tumor types beyond melanoma.

items.title: AbbVie’s skin disease drug lessens abscess burden in Phase 3 but falls below expectations
items.snippet: AbbVie is eyeing regulatory filings in 2027 for the skin disease drug lutikizumab after clearing multiple endpoints in a late-stage trial, but the results have disappointed some analysts, raising questions about its commercial prospects.

items.title: Biohaven shares pop as FDA accepts resubmission for ataxia drug with adcomm expected
items.snippet: Troriluzole, in development for spinocerebellar ataxia, was rejected nearly a year ago when the FDA took issue with the design of Biohaven’s registrational study. The agency has now agreed to review a new application and render a decision in the first quarter of 2027.

items.title: Biotech notches 31 IPOs already this year, with 4 more joining queue
items.snippet: The sector’s IPO tally has surpassed each of the past four years, with four October debuts adding momentum—but activity still remains well below the COVID-19 boom that saw nearly 100 public debuts in 2021.

items.title: GSK, Ionis hepatitis B functional cure breaks open market for followers
items.snippet: The approval of Hibsago has created a new market for a handful of biopharmas, including Gilead, Arrowhead, and Vir, to fill in.

items.title: Roche’s pipeline trim claims Poseida’s off-the-shelf CAR T asset
items.snippet: Aside from RG6540, Roche also discontinued a host of other early-stage assets, including an antisense oligonucleotide for Alzheimer’s disease and a small-molecule candidate for geographic atrophy.

items.title: Why investors are taking another look at kidney disease
items.snippet: In this episode of Denatured, you’ll hear from Bruce Culleton, CEO at ProKidney and Demetri Maxim, CEO at Nephrogen. We discuss why kidney disease has long been a hard target for cell and gene therapies, and what new delivery strategies, therapeutic approaches and regulatory clarity mean for commercially viable produc...

items.title: Roivant's TYK2/JAK inhibitor reduces need for steroids in inflammatory eye disease
items.snippet: Brepocitinib is on a roll. After winning approval for an autoimmune skin disease, Roivant Sciences subsidiary Priovant’s drug hit all primary and secondary endpoints in a pair of Phase 3 non-infectious uveitis trials, leading analysts to say the candidate “looked superior to Humira.”

items.title: Critical decisions that spurred these 40 Under 40 winners to success
items.snippet: Securing financing that allowed an exit from academia, leaving ecology and evolutionary biology for biomedical engineering and shifting from business development to entrepreneurship are among key turning points for three biopharma professionals.

items.title: As H-1B visa changes keep coming, biopharmas adjust hiring approach
items.snippet: The $100,000 H-1B visa fee has significantly affected who biopharma companies hire, according to two experts. It’s not the only program adjustment affecting foreign-born job seekers’ odds of working in the U.S.

items.title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
items.snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
